Note::to_ascii¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::to_ascii() const

Replace Every Non-ASCII Character With ?¶

to_ascii() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, in which ASCII bytes pass through and each non-ASCII character is replaced by a single ?. Use it when a downstream system is strictly ASCII and you want a visible, fixed-width marker for every character that could not be represented, rather than silently dropping it.

The replacement is per character, not per byte: a two- or three-byte UTF-8 character becomes one ?, so "café" is four characters and yields "caf?". This is a lossy conversion and not a transliteration — it does not know that é “means” e. When you want accented letters folded to their base ASCII forms (café → cafe), use transliterate_ascii(); when you want non-ASCII simply removed with no marker, use keep_ascii.

to_ascii is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"café résumé", "naïve", "日本語", "plain"}).to_ascii())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["caf? r?sum?", "na?ve", "???", "plain"]

Each accented letter and each CJK character becomes one ?; "plain" is untouched.

See Also¶

  • pluss::coden::Note::transliterate_ascii: fold non-ASCII to ASCII equivalents instead of marking them.

  • Note::keep_ascii: drop non-ASCII with no replacement marker.

  • Note::is_ascii: test whether a cell is already pure ASCII.
